Web design Wilmington NC owners need has to work for two different people. One is the visitor in June who just crossed the bridge to Wrightsville Beach and wants a kayak rental, a fish taco or a sitter for the kids. The other is the neighbor in January who needs a plumber, a vet or a haircut and has lived here for twenty years. Most local sites only talk to one of them.

To be clear for searchers: this page is about Wilmington, North Carolina, not Wilmington, Delaware. Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds every site by hand from East Texas, shows you a free demo before you pay, and charges a printed one-time price.

Web design in Wilmington, NC for a town with two seasons

Tourism is big here, and it is measured. Visitors spent about $1.2 billion in New Hanover County in 2025, up 5.8% from the year before, which put the county seventh among North Carolina's 100 counties. In 2024 food and beverage was the largest spending category, with restaurants alone above $350 million, and tourism supported about 7,000 jobs in the county.

Those dollars arrive in waves. Carolina Beach and Kure Beach fill up on summer weekends, charter boats book out, short-term rentals turn over every few days. After Labor Day, much of the visitor trade thins and the local customer carries the business until spring.

Think of a rental turnover cleaner. In July the site needs a fast quote form for property managers and a clear list of the beach towns covered. In February it should talk to year-round homeowners about deep cleans and move-outs. Same business, same phone number, a different front page.

A website that never changes its message is stuck in one season. Planning for both from the start costs nothing extra; it just takes a designer who asks how your year actually goes.

How one coastal site can switch with the season

  1. Spring, before the crowdsOpen bookings for summer, post your season hours and refresh photos while people are still planning their trips.
  2. Summer, at full speedKeep the top of the home page short: hours, a map, a tap-to-call button and what is available this week. Visitors decide in seconds.
  3. Fall, the turnSwap visitor offers for local ones: lessons, maintenance plans, gift cards, a loyalty line for neighbors.
  4. Winter, the quiet monthsWrite the pages you never have time for in July, such as a service page for each area you cover. If a storm closes you for a day, the same notice spot tells customers when you reopen.

Website design Wilmington NC film crews and vendors can use

Wilmington's screen industry started with one movie. Frank Capra Jr. scouted the area in 1983 for Firestarter, made for Dino De Laurentiis, and De Laurentiis then built a studio near the airport. The studio changed hands several times, became EUE/Screen Gems after 1996, and in 2023 was sold to Cinespace, which runs it as Cinespace Wilmington.

The work comes and goes. The Wilmington Regional Film Commission's director estimated about $30 million in local production spending in 2025, against roughly $200 million the year before, and the state budget signed in 2026 raised the maximum production grant from $7 million to $20 million to win more shoots back.

That swing is exactly why a freelancer or vendor here needs a simple site. Grips, caterers, prop and equipment rentals, set carpenters and still photographers who work productions also take local jobs between them. One page set can serve both: a production-facing page with credits you are allowed to name, services and the counties you will travel to, and a local page for weddings, events or home projects.

Wilmington website design that names the places people say

The city had about 122,700 residents in the Census Bureau's 2023 estimate, but the customer base runs well past the city line, and people search by the name of their own spot on the map.

  • Downtown and the Riverwalk, which runs 1.75 miles along the Cape Fear River through the historic district.
  • The Cargo District, begun in 2017 with small, locally owned businesses in converted shipping containers; its developer said in 2025 that about 85 businesses rent space there, roughly 19 of them restaurants and nine of them bars.
  • Market Street and Oleander Drive, two long commercial corridors, and the Ogden area farther out Market Street.
  • Monkey Junction, the unincorporated crossroads where Carolina Beach Road meets College Road.
  • Leland across the river, now the largest town in Brunswick County at about 34,450 people in the 2024 estimate, and Hampstead up the coast in Pender County.

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. A page that truthfully says you serve Leland, Hampstead or Monkey Junction gives Google a reason to match you when someone there searches. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each one researched and written about that place. Owners serving more of the coast, the kind who search "web design nc" rather than a city name, can use Agency, which starts with keyword research across the whole area.

A university town on top of a beach town

UNC Wilmington (UNCW) reported 19,895 students in fall 2025 by preliminary count, with 3,109 first-year students, the largest incoming class in its history. Students and their families are customers for apartments, food, haircuts, car repair and pet care, and the academic calendar adds its own rhythm to the year.

Year-round appointment businesses, such as a veterinary clinic, a dentist or a tutor, gain the most from steady pages: services spelled out, a booking request form, the parking situation and the neighborhoods served. They are the shops the January neighbor is looking for.

Move-in week in August and graduation in May are worth a seasonal note too, if they change your hours or your rush.

Wilmington Chamber of CommerceFounded in 1853, and described by a 2003 state House resolution as the oldest chamber in North Carolina.

Common questions

How much does web design cost in Wilmington, NC?

Quotes vary widely with who builds the site and how much is custom, and many firms only give a number after a meeting. Ours are printed: $497 for the 5-page Starter, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency, each paid once. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent, so a seasonal owner can plan the yearly cost before spending a dollar.

Is this page about Wilmington, North Carolina or Wilmington, Delaware?

Wilmington, North Carolina: the port city on the Cape Fear River in New Hanover County, with Wrightsville, Carolina and Kure beaches nearby. The two are easy to mix up in search results. If your business is in Delaware, the rest of our site still applies, but the local details here do not.

Can a charter, surf or rental business keep a website useful in the off-season?

Yes, and it should. In winter the same site can push gift cards, early booking for next summer, lessons for locals or a shorter schedule. The key is a front page that can change its message by season, and someone who will make that change when you ask. On our hosting plan, that is us.

Do you offer website development in Wilmington, NC, or only design?

We design, write and build the site, set up the contact form, page titles, descriptions, sitemap and schema, and host it. That covers what most small Wilmington businesses need. Custom software, such as a booking engine tied to your own reservation database, belongs with a development firm, and we will tell you so up front.

Should a film crew freelancer or production vendor have a website?

A small one is worth it. Producers and coordinators often check a vendor online before calling, so a page that shows your work, the gear or services you offer, the counties you cover and a phone number that rings is enough. It also keeps you findable for local customers between productions.

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
